title: Calzone
subtitle: Stuffed Italian pizza parcels with ricotta, spinach, and pancetta
excerpt: A calzone is a folded pizza that bakes into a golden, puffed parcel with a molten, creamy filling. This version uses ricotta, mozzarella, wilted spinach, and salty pancetta. The dough is the same as a standard pizza base, risen before shaping. Great for feeding a crowd.
sourceNotes: Follows southern Italian calzone tradition. The ricotta and spinach filling is a classic Neapolitan combination.

content.text: Squeeze the spinach very thoroughly before mixing it into the filling. Any water left in the leaves will make the filling watery and cause the dough to tear when it bakes.
Mix the bread flour with 7g fast-action yeast, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp olive oil, and 320ml warm water. Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.

Fry the pancetta in a dry pan over medium heat until lightly crisp. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Remove from the heat and cool slightly. Mix together the ricotta, mozzarella, spinach, and pancetta mixture. Season well.
Heat the oven to 220C. Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Roll each piece into a circle about 25cm across. Spoon filling onto one half of each circle, leaving a 2cm border.
Fold the dough over to make a half-moon. Press and crimp the edges firmly to seal. Place on oiled baking trays. Brush the tops with the remaining olive oil and cut a small steam vent in each.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Leave to rest for 3 minutes before serving.

items.fix: Crimp edges more firmly and check for any gaps.

items.symptom: Dough is raw at the edges.
items.cause: Filling packed too close to the border.
items.fix: Keep filling away from the last 2cm of dough.
Squeeze the spinach well before mixing it in.
